samples.identification: Salat Go RAT and credential stealer
samples.marker_line: Salat RAT: steals credentials and keystrokes; adds persistence coverage
evidence: Unsigned 32-bit Windows GUI PE, Go 1.24.0 module salat, no Authenticode security directory. Overlay is 286 bytes and contains GBZAP marker strings; it is not a signature or a reason to infer additional malicious actions.

Recovered Go pclntab with debug/gosym; disassembled instructions with Rizin and Capstone. main.main starts the task loop; main.tloop parses responses and dispatches main.doTask. Its wrappers reach main.Steal, main.sendScreen, main.shellCommand, and main.p2pSocks.

main.getChromeLogins at 0x8f2dc0 opens the browser SQLite database, selects login rows, scans them, invokes main.DecryptChrome, and formats URL/Login/Password records. main.Steal at 0x8e5b30 stages browser credentials/cookies, Telegram tdata, wallet extension stores and Steam/session files into a ZIP, then calls main.rq. Firefox key4/NSS decryption is also implemented.

main.keyPressCallback at 0x8d17e0 translates keyboard events and writes to a buffered recorder. main.runKeylogger at 0x8d1e30 opens its log and installs the keyboard hook. main.sendScreen at 0x8d2410 obtains a screen image, encodes Base64, serializes JSON and passes it to main.rq.

main.staticinstall at 0x8da540 copies the executable, attempts main.newTask, and falls back to HKCU SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run using registry.CreateKey and registry.Key.setStringValue. The copied file may be marked hidden/system. main.newTask at 0x8db580 builds an executable action and time/repetition triggers and calls TaskService.CreateTask.

main.decryptAPPB reaches main.impersonateSystem. main.getSystemToken at 0x8f9300 enables privilege, finds LSASS, opens its token, and calls DuplicateTokenEx; main.impersonateSystem at 0x8f9660 invokes the impersonation API. These are credential-boundary operations, not proof of initial elevation success.

Configuration recovery: reconstruct 129-word obfuscated integers with rotate/XOR, apply modular exponent 65537 with a recovered 4096-bit modulus, decode hex and cumulative XOR, XOR with an AES-decrypted static mask, decode hex and decrypt AES-GCM. AES key is cumulative-XOR(MD5(biba)). Four C2 URLs were independently recovered; no endpoint was contacted.

Downloaded Triage HTML corroborates browser/wallet access, UAC-related behavior and Salat identification, but the verdict rests on executable code. There is no evidence of a legitimate signed product or an authorized deployment in the supplied context.
samples.coverage: All original findings retained. Two distinct hostile findings added: logon Run-key persistence and LSASS SYSTEM-token impersonation.

samples.marker_line: Runner stealer JS: attempts memory-secret export; fixes rule claims
evidence: Both files represent the same shell command; JavaScript invokes it at module load with child_process.execSync. The JavaScript literal was decoded before examining shell semantics.

Pipeline: curl Gist API -> jq extracts a Python member content -> sudo python3 -> tr -> grep for value/isSecret:true records -> sort -u -> base64 -w 0 -> variable. A second curl posts that variable as the GitHub issue body, authenticating with GITHUB_TOKEN.

Fetched Gist snapshot and .forage.json retained in scratch. Its memdump.py selects /proc cmdline containing Runner.Worker, reads maps and memory, seeks readable regions, and sends raw bytes to stdout. The mutable Gist is supporting evidence; its historical contents at deployment are unknown.

An inert command harness replaced curl, jq and sudo; it never executed downloaded code or performed network activity. The exact shell arguments in both samples contain an overescaped grep expression which did not match a normal Runner secret record canary; the attempted POST then had an empty body. tr also receives an overescaped deletion expression. This prevents claiming successful secret export, but does not erase the deliberate secret-export attempt.

No package manifest, install hook, repository compromise, successful sudo, valid GitHub token, or API acceptance is supplied. A deliberate privileged runner-memory-to-issue pipeline tips the verdict to malicious even with execution defects.
samples.coverage: One local hostile composite describes the distinct supported theft/export chain. The generic downloader alone is neutral. A second local hostile trait would reassert that same chain or guess downloaded behavior from a chosen filename; this is an evidence-supported minimum-count gap. The separately fetched Python stage has two hostile memory-acquisition findings and one suspicious finding.
samples.classifier_disagreement: Current classifier has no calibrated alert (level -1) despite high raw probability and a hostile trait. Live JavaScript terminal output says BENIGN[50%] and all clean. Shell also exits 0 with level -1. Supplied public HOSTILE prior is not this local calibrated result.

rule_corrections.reason: A curl command mentioning a chosen memdump.py filename plus separate sudo interpreter text establishes neither a GitHub runner dump nor hostile intent. Existing notable atoms retain both observations, and existing consumers directly require the same two facts. Add a bound JSON-content-to-sudo-Python deployment matcher without the chosen filename.

Relocate source-plus-send behavior to exfiltration/stealer/dev-secret. Require actual secret filtering and describe co-occurrence/attempt rather than successful memory exfiltration. No supply-chain substitution or trust violation is established.

Old matcher required only the api.github.com root, so Gist requests were mislabeled as release downloads. Restrict to /repos/owner/repo/releases and place the retained reference under http/client/service.
Replace incorrect perl description with the actual uniq/tr pipeline claim; matcher and severity unchanged.
Description now says tool-name reference, not a proven command invocation.

Extend existing API atoms to the qualified compiled Go calls recovered in file facts; preserve original API spellings and neutral criticalities. New hostile composites add independent theft, LSASS/impersonation, or Run-key context.

shared_rule_review: Inspected all exact consumers of removed/moved IDs and API atoms. Other pipeline consumers directly retain the old exact two-fact evidence. No package-specific exceptions, demotions to hide signal, or score-driven duplicates added.

verification.retained_external_positive: testdata/hostile/memdump.py.xz: all 30 findings identical before/after on container and memdump.py archive member, including 2 hostile and 1 suspicious findings.
verification.controls: Renamed Python member retains theft detection; ordinary bootstrap, comment-only pipelines, Gist queries, release queries and ordinary token/registry APIs have no hostile findings. Release queries retain the corrected notable API reference.
verification.original_samples: Each original has atomscan before/after and cleave facts including decoded literals in scratch. Original samples are not archives.
verification.material_losses: PE: none. Scripts: unsupported standalone hostile downloader replaced with notable evidence; existing hostile export relocated; false release label removed from shell. The observed attack remains detected.
verification.engine_warning: Local model feature spec v18 is older than extractor v19. This is reported without asserting it causes the classifier misses.
